episode_title: #135 Jennifer Davis, Tech Entrepreneur and Business Titan, Running for Congress!

real_qa.q: What problem did Davisware solve for heating and air conditioning service companies?
real_qa.r: Davisware solved the core logistical problem of trades: getting the right person to the right place at the right time with the right parts and skills. The software replaced manual T-card dispatching systems with integrated dispatch boards, billing, inventory, GPS, and accounting systems. Jennifer Davis emphasized focusing on first-time fix rates by building massive databases to match technician skill sets and truck inventory with predicted customer problems based on equipment models.

real_qa.q: What is the annual cost and return on investment for small HVAC companies using Davisware?
real_qa.r: For a five to six million dollar HVAC startup, annual costs were approximately $7,000 to $8,000 per month under the SaaS model, though legacy customers paid $150,000 to $200,000 upfront with 18% to 22% annual maintenance. Companies could reduce parts inventory on trucks by 50%, reduce back-office staff ratios from 1:1 to 3:1 or 4:1 technician-to-support ratios, thereby saving hundreds of thousands of dollars while increasing revenue opportunities.

real_qa.q: What industries did Davisware expand into beyond HVAC?
real_qa.r: Davisware expanded into commercial food equipment service, petroleum equipment service for gas stations, and doors and docks. The company targeted industries with complex parts having serial numbers, regulatory requirements, and high stakes for error—food equipment service where mistakes cause illness, petroleum equipment where mistakes cause explosions. The software became particularly successful with customers like Partstown that operated both distribution and service operations.
real_qa.requete: Davisware industries food service petroleum equipment

real_qa.q: When did Jennifer Davis and Dan Davis sell Davisware and to whom?
real_qa.r: Jennifer Davis and her husband Dan sold Davisware in July 2019 to Sareint Capital, a private equity firm specializing in field service software investments. Jennifer remained in an operating role until January 2023 and stayed on the board until April 2025 when Sareint Capital sold the company to ECI, a Dallas-based field service software company that continues servicing the same industries.

real_qa.q: What remote work and company culture practices did Davisware implement early?
real_qa.r: Davisware hired its first remote employee in 1991, decades before remote work became standard, which created a decade-long tax dispute between Illinois and Ohio. The company required cameras on for all meetings with two or more people, and required phone calls instead of email chains after three consecutive emails. They held annual user conferences where every employee attended, closing support lines to emphasize company mission and culture.

guest.bio_context: Jennifer Davis grew up as the sixth of nine children on a farm in rural Wisconsin. At age 17, she met her now-husband Dan and began building a technology business while still in college, studying elementary education at the University of Wisconsin. She and Dan built Davisware from a college startup into a comprehensive field service software platform serving HVAC, food equipment service, and petroleum equipment industries. The company achieved over 95% customer retention and was sold to Sareint Capital in July 2019, later acquired by ECI in April 2025. She has since transitioned into political life, running for Congress in Illinois's 8th congressional district.
